entries.697e2428095273f3: Under its long-term vision toward 2050, “BLUE MISSION 2050,” it aims to achieve carbon neutrality in the Power Generation Business and, to accelerate efforts from 2030 onward, to transform its business portfolio in Japan and overseas, centered on carbon-neutral assets. The key priorities of the Medium-Term Management Plan (2024–2026) are establishing and growing sustainable revenue sources (domestic renewable energy business and Overseas Business); laying the groundwork for the business portfolio of the 2030s (CO2-free hydrogen and ammonia strategy, contributing to strengthening power networks, promoting the Ohma Nuclear Power Plant project, and creating new business domains); improving profitability and investment efficiency; strengthening group competitiveness; and deepening ESG management. As a non-financial target, it aims to reduce CO2 emissions from domestic power generation by 22.5 million t (46%) by 2030 compared with fiscal 2013.

entries.734e67d7c2ba145e: This reportable segment covers power generation by the company or its affiliates, including hydroelectric, thermal and wind power, along with their maintenance and operation, and the sale of electricity procured from the wholesale electricity trading market and other sources. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥840,445 million, the largest of the five reportable segments. Electricity sold in the same fiscal year was 66.7 billion kWh, down 1.7% from the previous year. This comprised 9.8 billion kWh from renewable energy, 41.8 billion kWh from thermal power, and 15 billion kWh of electricity procured from the wholesale electricity trading market and other sources. Revenue including intersegment internal revenue fell 10.5% from the previous year, due to the decommissioning of the Matsushima Thermal Power Station and a decline in capacity market prices. As of March 31, 2026, the company's facilities comprised 61 hydroelectric power stations, 7 steam power stations, and 2 power stations for new energy and other sources. Major customers are the Japan Electric Power Exchange (revenue ¥191,732 million) and The Chugoku Electric Power Co., Inc. (revenue ¥121,889 million).
